prediction.reasoning: Rear view of a heavy commercial truck cab and bare chassis at what appears to be a heavy-truck equipment dealer lot (other conventional tractors visible in background). The cab is a small, square, flat-backed unit typical of a cabover/vocational tractor with no sleeper bunk bulge visible. Behind the cab is an exposed heavy frame with a tandem set of dual rear wheels (two axles, four tires per side) and visible air/hydraulic lines and a mudflap set branded for a heavy equipment dealer. The scale of the cab relative to the tires and frame, plus the tandem dual-wheel axle group, are consistent with a Class 7/8 day-cab tractor chassis rather than any medium-duty pickup or van.

Primary subject is a Freightliner conventional truck (badge visible on grille) with a tall day-cab (no sleeper bunk visible), large chrome grille, and a heavy dump body mounted directly behind the cab, visible tandem axle housing near the rear wheels. The cab height, hood length, and step/fuel tank proportions match a heavy Class 7/8 tractor/dump chassis, not a medium-duty pickup or box truck.

Rear-facing shot of a heavy chassis with an exposed fifth-wheel-style pivot plate and a blue dump/hopper body above it, sitting on a tandem set of dual rear wheels (four tires visible per side). The heavy frame rails, tandem duals, air lines, and dump body scale are consistent with a Class 7/8 heavy dump truck, not a medium-duty stake or flatbed truck.

Rear view of a heavy truck showing a tall gray dump/hopper body mounted on a heavy chassis with a tandem set of dual rear wheels (four large commercial tires visible per side) and a fifth-wheel-style pivot area with hydraulic lines. The wheel/tire scale, dual-axle rear end, and heavy dump body are consistent with a Class 7/8 heavy dump truck rather than any medium-duty vehicle.

Rear view of a black stake/dump-style body with a rear tailgate, chains, and reflective conspicuity striping, sitting low to the ground with a compact rear bumper marked 'Sterling Trucks'. No dual rear wheels or tandem axle group are visible, the body width and bumper/step proportions read as a single rear axle, and the overall scale is noticeably smaller than a true Class 7/8 dump body. These cues point to a medium-duty (Class 2-6) stake or dump body rather than a Class 7/8 tractor or heavy dump truck, so per the guidance to prefer invalid when heavy-duty cues do not clearly dominate, this is classified as invalid.
